pathway.title: Oceaneering International Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Liquidity and leverage are the strongest support. Debt at carrying value is USD 491.42 million against cash of USD 734.94 million, which is net cash of USD 243.52 million, and cash still exceeds the USD 500 million principal of the notes by USD 234.94 million; with the undrawn revolving facility, liquidity is USD 1,079.94 million, and the annual coupon of USD 34.38 million is covered 11.23x by last-twelve-month reported EBITDA. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19

- Earnings have improved but rest on one segment and one cycle. Operating margin rose from 7.48% in 2023 to 10.94% in 2025, led by Subsea Robotics (margin 23.16% to 30.06%) and Manufactured Products (7.20% to 12.74%), yet Subsea Robotics supplies 52.03% of segment operating income on 30.72% of revenue and Energy customers generate 83.48% of revenue. Volume did not drive the gain: ROV utilization was 65% in 2025 against 67% and 64% in the nine months of 2026 against 66%, so the margin came from day rates and mix. Basis: calculation B1; calculation B2; calculation B3; calculation B4; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 112–113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33

- Cash conversion is volatile and guided sharply lower for 2026. Free cash flow was USD 207.85 million in 2025, 51.77% of adjusted EBITDA, and USD 288.11 million over the last twelve months, 70.61% of USD 408.03 million, but the fourth quarter of 2025 alone supplied USD 190.69 million, so the twelve-month figure overstates the run rate. The 2026 guide of USD 100 million to USD 120 million is 42.26% to 51.89% below 2025 and 24.84% to 29.09% of implied adjusted EBITDA, with USD 97.43 million earned in nine months and only USD 2.58 million to USD 22.58 million implied for the fourth quarter. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B5; calculation B6; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 10

- Revenue visibility is adequate but uneven. Firm backlog of USD 2,703 million at 2025-12-31 is 0.97x of 2025 revenue and 10.82% higher than a year earlier, and Aerospace and Defense holds USD 658 million of unfunded orders outside it, but Manufactured Products backlog fell 23.42% in the twelve months to 2026-09-30 and management expects Offshore Projects Group and Subsea Robotics operating income to be lower in the fourth quarter. Basis: calculation B10; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 2

- Cash flow quality is thinner than the free cash flow headline. Receivables and contract assets absorbed USD 139.06 million in the first nine months of 2026 while operating cash flow still rose on higher current liabilities and non-cash items, and contract liabilities of USD 135.30 million equal 18.41% of cash, so a reversal of prepayments would be a call on cash. Basis: calculation B8; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

- The outlook is flat for 2026 and higher for 2027 on management guidance. Fourth-quarter EBITDA of USD 85 million to USD 95 million leaves implied 2026 adjusted EBITDA of USD 402.54 million to USD 412.54 million against USD 408.03 million for the last twelve months, while 2027 is guided at USD 430 million to USD 480 million, 5.38% to 17.64% higher. Company-cited industry data are mixed: contracted floating rigs fell 6.2% in 2025, but subsea tree awards are projected 61.05% higher in 2026. Basis: calculation B6; calculation B12; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 55

- Refinancing risk is low, but the ranking of the notes and claims outside debt are open. The only debt is the 2034 notes, the revolving facility is undrawn and runs to 2031, and the refinancing raised the coupon by 87.5 bp, USD 4.38 million a year; outside the notes sit purchase obligations of USD 410.53 million, lease payments of USD 453.08 million and letters of credit of USD 77 million, and the notes' security and guarantors are not stated. Basis: calculation B11; calculation B13; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109

- Financial policy has been creditor-aligned on conduct. No dividend has been declared since 2017 and repurchases of USD 75.37 million since 2024 were 12.63% of 2025 and 9.46% of nine-month 2026 operating cash flow; no sponsor or controlling holder is identified, so any extraction risk comes from board policy, which the credit documents are not supplied to test. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B9; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44

runs.text: - Net cash and liquidity are the main strength: cash of USD 734.94 million exceeds debt of USD 491.42 million, the undrawn revolving facility adds USD 345 million and liquidity is USD 1,079.94 million, so the only debt, due in 2034, can be met from cash on hand with USD 234.94 million to spare and any 2026 to 2027 shortfall in free cash flow would be absorbed without borrowing. Basis: calculation B7; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

- Margins have been rising on price: operating margin went from 7.48% in 2023 to 10.94% in 2025 and Subsea Robotics from 23.16% to 30.06%, which lifts cash generation per unit of activity and supports debt service if prices hold. Basis: calculation B1; calculation B2; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 112–113

- Scale and technology give the company a defensible position, on its own account: it states it is the largest owner and operator of work-class ROVs in energy use, and its umbilicals, subsea hardware, inspection and defense engineering spread revenue over five segments. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11

- Backlog and government demand support visibility: firm backlog of USD 2,703 million is 0.97x of 2025 revenue and Aerospace and Defense holds USD 658 million of unfunded orders, which cushions the first year of any downturn. Basis: calculation B10; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14

- Financial policy is restrained: no dividend since 2017, repurchases of USD 75.37 million paid from cash flow, and no sponsor to extract value, which keeps cash available to creditors. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B9

- Earnings are cyclical and concentrated: Subsea Robotics earns 52.03% of segment operating income, ROV utilization has slipped to 64% from 66%, and fourth-quarter operating income is guided lower in that segment and in Offshore Projects Group, so a drop in offshore spending reaches the profit center first. Basis: calculation B3; calculation B4; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

- Weaker segments and orders: Integrity Management & Digital Solutions earned a margin of 3.78% in 2025 and Manufactured Products backlog fell 23.42% in the twelve months to 2026-09-30, so two of five segments are not carrying growth. Basis: calculation B2; calculation B10; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

- Cash conversion is volatile and depends on working capital: 2026 free cash flow is guided 42.26% to 51.89% below 2025, contract liabilities of USD 135.30 million equal 18.41% of cash and receivables absorbed USD 139.06 million in nine months, so operating cash flow can swing quickly with collections and prepayments. Basis: calculation B5; calculation B8; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 10

- The legal structure is not shown: the ranking, guarantors and security of the 2034 notes are not stated, and purchase obligations of USD 410.53 million, lease payments of USD 453.08 million and letters of credit of USD 77 million sit outside the debt figure. Basis: calculation B11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109

- Near-term momentum is flat: fourth-quarter EBITDA is guided at USD 85 million to USD 95 million against USD 87.77 million a year earlier, so the implied 2026 adjusted EBITDA of USD 402.54 million to USD 412.54 million is level with the last twelve months and growth rests on the 2027 guide. Basis: calculation B6; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 2

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The one transaction in the period is the refinancing completed on 2026-07-06. The company placed USD 500 million of senior notes due 2034 at a coupon above that of the 2028 notes, with proceeds of about USD 491 million after discounts and expenses, and used them with cash on hand to buy about USD 397 million of the USD 500 million 2028 notes in a tender offer for about USD 414 million including accrued interest; it redeemed the remainder on 2026-07-25 at principal, accrued interest and a make-whole premium of USD 1.9 million. Cash paid to retire the old notes exceeded the new notes' proceeds by USD 18.14 million, and the loss on extinguishment was USD 19.03 million. Basis: calculation A13; calculation A14; calculation A15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18

The revolving credit facility was amended the same day: commitments rose from USD 215 million to USD 345 million, maturity moved from April 2027 to July 2031 and margins fell by 25 bp at both ends of each range. It remains guaranteed by certain wholly owned subsidiaries and secured by first-priority liens on certain assets, with no borrowings and no letters of credit outstanding under the facility at 2026-09-30. The security and guarantors of the 2034 notes are not stated; their indenture limits secured debt to the greater of USD 350 million and the company's EBITDA as defined there, which replaces the asset-based test in the 2028 indenture, and the definitions needed to compute either limit are not supplied. Basis: calculation A16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–20; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 65

The only acquisition in the sources is GDi in October 2024, for approximately USD 33 million including a USD 4.6 million holdback, of which USD 27.15 million was paid in cash net of cash acquired; no sale, merger or ownership transaction is described. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_oii-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2024-12-31_oii-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84

fields.value: - The third-quarter report controls debt terms. The 2025 annual report still shows the 2028 notes as the nearest maturity and a revolving facility of USD 215 million maturing in April 2027; the July 2026 notes offering, tender offer and amendment supersede both.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Letters of credit are the liquidity input the sources do not close. The 2025 annual report states USD 77 million outstanding at 2025-12-31 outside the revolving facility, no later total is printed, and the third-quarter report states only that USD 8.5 million of restricted cash backs letters of credit and corporate cards.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant terms are summarised, not documented. The revolving facility requires net leverage of no more than 3.25x and interest coverage of at least 3.00x, tested quarterly, and the issuer reports compliance, but neither the definitions nor the issuer's own ratio levels are printed, so any headroom is an estimate on statement figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Two small disagreements inside the filings are kept visible. The tender offer is described as about USD 397 million of 2028 notes in the debt note and about USD 400 million in the liquidity discussion, and the 2034 notes proceeds are about USD 492 million in the second-quarter report and about USD 491 million in the third-quarter report, where the later figure agrees to the cash flow statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against sufficiency is that a secured revolving facility ranking ahead of unsecured notes is normally judged from the executed documents, and none is supplied: the filing summaries could omit a lien basket, a definition or a guarantor that matters to creditors. Supplying the credit agreement with both amendments and the indenture for the 2034 notes would move the covenant and structural work from summary to document, and a filing after 2026-10-22 that changes the debt terms would reopen the current-terms finding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No executed credit agreement or indenture is supplied, so covenant definitions, lien baskets and guarantor scope rest on the issuer's summaries; this limits any covenant headroom conclusion to the issuer's statement that it complies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit rating or bond price is supplied, and equity prices appear only as the issuer's average repurchase prices in August and September 2026 and a mid-2025 closing price, so rating and market-implied conclusions cannot be drawn from this evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so board composition, share ownership and executive pay are not established and governance conclusions rest on the annual report's officer biographies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The text conversion flattens tables and one row label is missing in the nine-month adjusted net income table of the third-quarter release, so adjusted net income lines must be tied to the statement totals before use.

fields.value: Each check uses amounts in USD thousand as printed unless stated; every difference is zero unless shown.

fields.value: The July 2026 refinancing was leverage-neutral but not cost-neutral: principal stayed at USD 500 million, the coupon rose by 87.5 bp and a USD 19.03 million loss on extinguishment was booked, which is why reported EBITDA of USD 385.96 million trails adjusted EBITDA of USD 408.03 million. Free cash flow is seasonal and guided lower for the fourth quarter, so the cash cushion is the point to monitor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation N4; calculation N5; calculation N7; calculation N11; calculation N15; Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is low and net debt is negative. Debt at carrying value of USD 491.42 million is 1.27x reported EBITDA and 1.20x adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months, and cash of USD 734.94 million leaves net cash of USD 243.52 million, up from USD 15.51 million at the end of 2024 and USD 201.46 million at the end of 2025. The improvement came from cash build, not repayment, because the debt is one bullet note whose carrying value moves only with the amortization of costs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation N4; calculation N5; calculation N7; calculation N10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reported EBITDA understates earnings momentum because of the refinancing. Fiscal 2025 reported EBITDA of USD 404.23 million compares with USD 385.96 million for the last twelve months, yet adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 401.47 million to USD 408.03 million; the USD 22.07 million gap between the two measures is mostly the USD 19.03 million loss on extinguishment of debt booked in the third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation N1; calculation N2; calculation N4; calculation N5; calculation N16; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Coverage is ample on every measure the sources allow. Fiscal 2025 reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 12.63x, last-twelve-month EBITDA covers interest expense 10.91x, and the annual coupon on the new notes of USD 34.38 million is covered 11.23x by reported EBITDA. Cash interest paid is not stated for interim periods, so the coupon cover is the only forward-looking measure available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation N4; calculation N11; calculation N12; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The refinancing extended maturities at a higher cost. Principal stayed at USD 500 million, the coupon rose by 87.5 bp and annual coupon interest rises by USD 4.38 million, while the revolving facility grew from USD 215 million to USD 345 million and now matures in 2031; no debt falls due before 2034.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation N11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow is strong over twelve months but seasonal and guided lower. Last-twelve-month operating cash flow of USD 380.25 million less capital spending of USD 92.14 million gives free cash flow of USD 288.11 million, yet nine-month 2026 free cash flow is USD 97.43 million and management guides full-year 2026 free cash flow of USD 100 million to USD 120 million, which implies only USD 2.58 million to USD 22.58 million in the fourth quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation N13; calculation N15; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash flow quality is thinner than the headline. Nine-month operating cash flow rose USD 61.39 million although net income fell USD 23.86 million, because current liabilities added USD 66.10 million and non-cash items USD 35.40 million while receivables and contract assets absorbed USD 42.63 million more than a year earlier; earnings did not drive the improvement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer prepayments are a float, not debt. Contract liabilities were USD 135.30 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 115.03 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 140.70 million at 2024-12-31, and receivables and contract assets absorbed USD 139.06 million in the nine months; if prepayments reverse or collections slip, the float turns into a call on cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation N18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 83

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is ample and no maturity falls before 2034. Cash of USD 734.94 million and an undrawn revolving facility of USD 345.00 million give liquidity of USD 1,079.94 million, with no letters of credit issued under the facility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation N14; calculation N20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The figures tie but three definitions need care. Reported EBITDA is the issuer's unadjusted measure and includes the loss on extinguishment, free cash flow excludes capitalised cloud costs, and fiscal 2024 EBITDA is calculated; the balance sheet balances and the cash flows foot in every column.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation N3; calculation N8; calculation N17; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against the benign view is that net cash is a seasonal high that may not persist. Cash fell by USD 81.40 million in the first quarter of 2026, nine-month free cash flow of USD 97.43 million came after receivables and contract assets absorbed USD 139.06 million, so a slip in collections would cut cash directly, and guidance implies fourth-quarter free cash flow of only USD 2.58 million to USD 22.58 million. Management also continues to repurchase shares and guides Offshore Projects Group operating income lower for the fourth quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would change if a cash drain of the size of the net cash, USD 243.52 million, became plausible: a fourth-quarter free cash flow below the guided range, a further receivables build, or debt-funded repurchases or acquisitions would be the observable signs. It would strengthen if year-end cash holds above the current balance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation N13; calculation N15; calculation N18; calculation N19; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid is stated only for fiscal years and rounded to USD millions, so interim cash interest cover is not stated and the interest-expense ratio is an accrual proxy that includes non-cash amortization; coverage conclusions for the last twelve months are approximate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Fiscal 2024 EBITDA is calculated with an amortization figure printed only to USD 0.1 million and the issuer states no fiscal 2024 adjusted EBITDA, so the year-on-year trend to fiscal 2025 carries that imprecision and has no adjusted comparison for 2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The security, guarantors and ranking of the senior notes are not stated, so no ranked debt stack is drawn and the notes are not placed against the secured revolving facility; leverage is on total carrying-value debt without seniority splits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Total letters of credit are not stated after 2025-12-31, so liquidity is cash plus undrawn commitments and is not shown net of any bonding or self-insurance lines outside the facility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Subsequent events are flagged by date and kept out of period figures: on 2026-07-06 the issuer placed the senior notes due 2034, entered Amendment No. 2 to the revolving credit agreement and repurchased most of the 2028 notes in a tender offer, and the remainder was called for redemption on 2026-07-25; the balance sheets at 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31, 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30 precede these events and the 2026-09-30 balance sheet follows them. No event after 2026-09-30 is stated.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings state the revolving facility's security and guarantors but not the senior notes', which are the whole debt, so no ranked stack is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The bridge covers nine months to 2026-09-30 and the two adjustments are the only ones the issuer states.

fields.value: Each line gives what is missing, the period, what it restricts, its severity and what would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no adjusted EBITDA for fiscal 2024 in the sources, so adjusted leverage and adjusted cover for FY2024 are not calculable. Severity Low; the 2024 fourth-quarter earnings release would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Fiscal 2024 EBITDA is calculated, not stated, and the amortization inside interest expense is printed only in USD millions, so the figure is accurate to about 0.1 million. Severity Low; the 2024 earnings reconciliation would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid is stated only for fiscal years and rounded to USD millions, so EBITDA over cash interest is not calculable for 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30 and the fiscal ratios carry that rounding. Severity Medium; the issuer's supplemental cash flow disclosure would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The total of letters of credit outstanding is stated for 2024-12-31 and 2025-12-31 only, so liquidity net of letters of credit is not stated for the 2026 balance-sheet dates; the revolving facility carries none of them. Severity Medium; a letters of credit and surety schedule would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The security, guarantors and ranking of the senior notes due 2034 are not stated, so the debt stack is not drawn and the notes cannot be placed against the secured revolving facility. Severity High; the indenture and guarantor list would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The carrying value of the senior notes is disclosed only inside total long-term debt, so the instrument register shows principal plus one financing cost adjustment. Severity Low; no action needed because the two lines reconcile to total debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant levels are stated but the issuer prints no reported ratio and no definition, so covenant headroom is not calculated and no capacity is inferred. Severity High; the credit agreement definitions and compliance certificate would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Purchase obligations and operating lease maturities are stated at 2025-12-31 only, so claims outside debt are not updated to 2026-09-30. Severity Medium; the next annual report would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The gain or loss on extinguishment of debt, the repurchase and issuance of senior notes, the revolving facility cost line and treasury stock purchases are not lines of every statement period, and the statements print a dash for some, so those cells are not stated rather than zero. Severity Low; no action needed because the fiscal totals reconcile.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash taxes paid are stated for fiscal years only, so interim cash taxes are not stated; the third-quarter report gives only a full-year 2026 estimate. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Balance sheets at 2025-03-31, 2025-06-30 and 2025-09-30 are not supplied, so leverage is not stated at those dates and last-twelve-month figures begin at 2026-03-31. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2028 notes repurchase is stated as about 397 million of principal in the debt note and about 400 million in the liquidity discussion, and the 2034 notes proceeds as about 492 million then about 491 million; both are carried and the cash flow figures are used. Severity Low; the filings' own rounding explains the differences.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No post-balance-sheet event after 2026-09-30 that changes net debt is stated in the sources read, so no pro forma figure is stated. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Oceaneering International Inc (issuer oii-73756), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit_snapshot (Full credit assessment). Scope: business, operating model, ownership and control, governance and financial-policy behavior, with the July 2026 refinancing as the transaction, from the eight supplied SEC filings and earnings releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Oceaneering is a listed public company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified in the documents supplied, so creditor risk sits in the company's own financial policy, which has been creditor-aligned: no dividend since 2017, modest buybacks and a voluntary refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation A10; calculation A13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main operating risk is concentration: Subsea Robotics produced 52.03% of segment operating income on 30.72% of 2025 revenue, and demand follows offshore energy spending. Legal capacity could not be tested because the credit agreement and indenture are not in the file, so the low reading rests on conduct.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A1; calculation A3; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified, so creditors have no sponsor to rely on for support and none to fear for extraction. The shares are listed on the New York Stock Exchange, no holder is named in the reports supplied, and the ownership table sits in a proxy statement that is not in the file; one consolidated subsidiary has a small minority interest. Decisions on distributions therefore rest with a board that, by its own account, reviews the dividend each quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Distributions have been restrained and funded from cash flow, which is the main creditor-aligned evidence. The board has declared no quarterly dividend since 2017; repurchases resumed in 2024 after none between 2016 and August 2024 and total USD 75.37 million to the third quarter of 2026. Purchases were 12.63% of operating cash flow in 2025 and 9.46% in the nine months to 2026-09-30, the revolving facility was undrawn at the 2024 and 2025 year ends and at 2026-09-30, and 49.99% of the original authorization is unused. The 2027 outlook says repurchases will continue, so the policy is restrained, not closed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A10; calculation A11; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2024-12-31_oii-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The July 2026 refinancing was voluntary, extended maturities and shows no priming or exchange behavior. The company issued USD 500 million of senior notes due 2034, bought about USD 397 million of the USD 500 million of 2028 notes in a tender offer for about USD 414 million including accrued interest, redeemed the rest at principal plus a make-whole premium, and enlarged the revolving facility from USD 215 million to USD 345 million with maturity moved to July 2031 and margins 25 bp lower. The cost was a USD 19.03 million loss on extinguishment and USD 18.14 million of cash paid beyond the new notes' proceeds, and the new notes carry a coupon 87.5 bp higher than the ones replaced; their ranking, guarantors and security are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A13; calculation A14; calculation A15; calculation A16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business is diversified by product line but its earnings are not: Subsea Robotics produced 52.03% of segment operating income on 30.72% of 2025 revenue, with a 30.06% operating margin against 3.78% in Integrity Management & Digital Solutions. Energy customers generate 83.48% of revenue, and the work-class ROV fleet was used 64% of available days in the nine months to 2026-09-30 against 66% a year earlier, mostly on lower US Gulf activity. Earnings therefore follow ROV utilization and day rates more than the five-segment structure suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A1; calculation A3; calculation A9; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue visibility is adequate but uneven. Firm backlog was USD 2,703 million at 2025-12-31, 0.97x of 2025 revenue and 10.82% above a year earlier, with 60.82% due within a year; unfunded Aerospace and Defense backlog of USD 658 million sits outside it and is 2.36x its year-earlier level. Manufactured Products is the weak spot: backlog fell to USD 435 million at 2026-09-30 from USD 568 million a year earlier and the 12-month book-to-bill was 0.77x, so orders are trailing revenue in that segment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A8; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32–34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer and geographic concentration is moderate and tied to energy spending. The five largest customers were 31% of 2025 revenue, four of them oil and gas producers and the fifth the US Government at 12%, and foreign operations were 58.75% of nine-month 2026 revenue, led by Africa at 13.33% and the United Kingdom at 13.32%. Energy services are generally priced on dayrates under contracts that run from under a year to several years, so a cut in producer spending can reach revenue quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A6; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Aerospace and Defense is growing but at a lower margin and with a dispute agreed in principle. Nine-month revenue rose 20.18% while operating margin fell to 9.83% from 13.08%, reflecting pass-through activity, program cost mix and a net USD 5.50 million accrual for a customer dispute that the company expects to settle over the life of a multi-year contract. The US Government is the segment's main customer and the largest single customer overall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A4; calculation A5; calculation A17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance disclosure supports monitoring, and no related-party item, sponsor fee or covenant waiver appears in the sources. The company files quarterly reports and earnings releases that reconcile its adjusted measures, its auditor reported effective internal control at 2025-12-31, and the finance chief role changed in 2026 without a stated effect on reporting. Charter provisions requiring an 80% vote for business combinations with related persons and allowing preferred stock to be issued without shareholder approval make a change of control harder; whether noteholders have change-of-control protection is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a low-risk reading is that documented conduct is not documented capacity. The board reviews the dividend every quarter, says repurchases will continue and restates a strategy of further acquisitions, while the credit agreement and indenture, which set the real limits on distributions, investments and secured debt, are not supplied; the secured-debt limit in the new 2034 indenture moved from an asset-based test to the greater of a fixed amount and EBITDA as the indenture defines it, and neither can be computed from the summaries. The refinancing also added USD 130 million of secured revolving capacity, which would rank ahead of any unsecured claims if drawn. The operating case is also weaker than the five-segment spread implies, because half of segment operating income comes from one segment, Subsea Robotics, whose fourth-quarter operating income is guided lower on weaker ROV utilization. A debt-funded acquisition, distributions larger than free cash flow, revolver borrowing to fund buybacks or a holder building a controlling position would move the view to medium, as would restricted-payment baskets that prove wide; baskets that prove tight would firm the low reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A3; calculation A16; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–20; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No beneficial ownership table is supplied, so the finding that no controlling or large holder is identified rests on what the annual and quarterly reports print; a filing showing a holder with a large stake would change the ownership conclusion from no control to a named holder whose intentions are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The restricted-payment, investment and lien baskets are not read, so the low governance and sponsor reading rests on conduct and cannot be turned into a statement of what the documents permit; permissive baskets would raise the level without any new behavior.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Backlog is stated by segment at year ends and, for Manufactured Products only, at 2026-09-30, so revenue cover for 2026 and 2027 is not updated for the other four segments and the visibility finding is dated 2025-12-31.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customers are named only as the US Government and an unnamed group of oil and gas producers, so single-producer exposure behind the 31% top-five share is not established, which limits how far the concentration finding can be taken.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Oceaneering presents low sponsor and governance risk on documented conduct. The key supported behavior is restrained distributions funded from cash flow and a voluntary refinancing that extended maturities, which matters because debt-funded distributions and priming are the usual ways governance erodes creditor recovery, and neither appears in the sources. Countervailing evidence is that legal capacity cannot be assessed and that repurchases are guided to continue; further analysis requires the credit agreement, the indenture and the proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A10; calculation A13; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–20; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The one transaction in the period is the refinancing completed on 2026-07-06. The company placed USD 500 million of senior notes due 2034 at a coupon above that of the 2028 notes, with proceeds of about USD 491 million after discounts and expenses, and used them with cash on hand to buy about USD 397 million of the USD 500 million 2028 notes in a tender offer for about USD 414 million including accrued interest; it redeemed the remainder on 2026-07-25 at principal, accrued interest and a make-whole premium of USD 1.9 million. Cash paid to retire the old notes exceeded the new notes' proceeds by USD 18.14 million, and the loss on extinguishment was USD 19.03 million.

fields.value: The revolving credit facility was amended the same day: commitments rose from USD 215 million to USD 345 million, maturity moved from April 2027 to July 2031 and margins fell by 25 bp at both ends of each range. It remains guaranteed by certain wholly owned subsidiaries and secured by first-priority liens on certain assets, with no borrowings and no letters of credit outstanding under the facility at 2026-09-30. The security and guarantors of the 2034 notes are not stated; their indenture limits secured debt to the greater of USD 350 million and the company's EBITDA as defined there, which replaces the asset-based test in the 2028 indenture, and the definitions needed to compute either limit are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Oceaneering International Inc (issuer oii-73756), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit_snapshot (Full credit assessment). Scope: fundamental credit synthesis of business risk, financial profile, outlook, downside and monitoring triggers from the eight supplied SEC filings and releases and the three earlier modules.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Oceaneering's fundamental credit profile is strong for a cyclical offshore services issuer, because cash of USD 734.94 million exceeds debt of USD 491.42 million and the only debt matures in 2034, so near-term default and refinancing risk is low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The weaknesses are earnings concentration and cash conversion, not leverage: demand follows offshore oil and gas spending, Subsea Robotics supplies 52.03% of segment operating income, 2026 free cash flow is guided at USD 100 million to USD 120 million against USD 207.85 million in 2025, and the ranking of the notes against the secured revolving facility is not established, so loss given default is not judged here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B3; calculation B5; calculation B6; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity and leverage are the strongest support. Debt at carrying value is USD 491.42 million against cash of USD 734.94 million, which is net cash of USD 243.52 million, and cash still exceeds the USD 500 million principal of the notes by USD 234.94 million; with the undrawn revolving facility, liquidity is USD 1,079.94 million, and the annual coupon of USD 34.38 million is covered 11.23x by last-twelve-month reported EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings have improved but rest on one segment and one cycle. Operating margin rose from 7.48% in 2023 to 10.94% in 2025, led by Subsea Robotics (margin 23.16% to 30.06%) and Manufactured Products (7.20% to 12.74%), yet Subsea Robotics supplies 52.03% of segment operating income on 30.72% of revenue and Energy customers generate 83.48% of revenue. Volume did not drive the gain: ROV utilization was 65% in 2025 against 67% and 64% in the nine months of 2026 against 66%, so the margin came from day rates and mix.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B1; calculation B2; calculation B3; calculation B4; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 112–113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash conversion is volatile and guided sharply lower for 2026. Free cash flow was USD 207.85 million in 2025, 51.77% of adjusted EBITDA, and USD 288.11 million over the last twelve months, 70.61% of USD 408.03 million, but the fourth quarter of 2025 alone supplied USD 190.69 million, so the twelve-month figure overstates the run rate. The 2026 guide of USD 100 million to USD 120 million is 42.26% to 51.89% below 2025 and 24.84% to 29.09% of implied adjusted EBITDA, with USD 97.43 million earned in nine months and only USD 2.58 million to USD 22.58 million implied for the fourth quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B5; calculation B6; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue visibility is adequate but uneven. Firm backlog of USD 2,703 million at 2025-12-31 is 0.97x of 2025 revenue and 10.82% higher than a year earlier, and Aerospace and Defense holds USD 658 million of unfunded orders outside it, but Manufactured Products backlog fell 23.42% in the twelve months to 2026-09-30 and management expects Offshore Projects Group and Subsea Robotics operating income to be lower in the fourth quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B10; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash flow quality is thinner than the free cash flow headline. Receivables and contract assets absorbed USD 139.06 million in the first nine months of 2026 while operating cash flow still rose on higher current liabilities and non-cash items, and contract liabilities of USD 135.30 million equal 18.41% of cash, so a reversal of prepayments would be a call on cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B8; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The outlook is flat for 2026 and higher for 2027 on management guidance. Fourth-quarter EBITDA of USD 85 million to USD 95 million leaves implied 2026 adjusted EBITDA of USD 402.54 million to USD 412.54 million against USD 408.03 million for the last twelve months, while 2027 is guided at USD 430 million to USD 480 million, 5.38% to 17.64% higher. Company-cited industry data are mixed: contracted floating rigs fell 6.2% in 2025, but subsea tree awards are projected 61.05% higher in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B6; calculation B12; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 55

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Refinancing risk is low, but the ranking of the notes and claims outside debt are open. The only debt is the 2034 notes, the revolving facility is undrawn and runs to 2031, and the refinancing raised the coupon by 87.5 bp, USD 4.38 million a year; outside the notes sit purchase obligations of USD 410.53 million, lease payments of USD 453.08 million and letters of credit of USD 77 million, and the notes' security and guarantors are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B11; calculation B13; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy has been creditor-aligned on conduct. No dividend has been declared since 2017 and repurchases of USD 75.37 million since 2024 were 12.63% of 2025 and 9.46% of nine-month 2026 operating cash flow; no sponsor or controlling holder is identified, so any extraction risk comes from board policy, which the credit documents are not supplied to test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B9; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a strong reading is that the balance sheet reflects a good cycle, not durable earnings power. Net cash of USD 243.52 million was built while contracted floating rigs fell 6.2% in 2025 and ROV utilization slipped two points, margins rose on price, and Subsea Robotics now earns 52.03% of segment operating income; a downturn in offshore spending would reach that segment through utilization first, with vessel charters, the fleet and unallocated costs largely fixed, and one point of utilization is about USD 10.75 million of annual ROV revenue. Free cash flow is guided to about half of the 2025 level and part of the cash is customer money, so the cushion could be thinner than it looks. The view would weaken if fourth-quarter EBITDA came in below USD 85 million, if the revolving facility were drawn, if buybacks or acquisitions were funded with debt, or if the documents placed the notes behind a larger secured facility; it would strengthen if the 2027 guide of USD 430 million to USD 480 million is met with utilization back above 65%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B3; calculation B4; calculation B6; calculation B7; calculation B12; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The ranking, guarantors and security of the 2034 notes against the secured revolving facility are not established, so this module judges default risk and liquidity but not loss given default; a junior ranking would lower the recovery reading without changing the default view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit rating, peer set or bond price is supplied, so the comparison of the business with other leveraged offshore issuers is qualitative and the adequacy of the profile is not benchmarked.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Forward evidence is management guidance for the fourth quarter of 2026, the full year 2026 and 2027, with no independent forecast, so the outlook conclusions assume the guidance is met.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The industry indicators for floating rigs and subsea trees are quoted by the company from third-party data that is not supplied, so the sector view is external and unverified here and would move if those data were wrong.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Operating lease liabilities are not discounted or split between current and long-term at 2026-09-30, so leverage including leases is not calculable and debt-based leverage understates the fixed claims from chartered vessels and other leases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Net cash and liquidity are the main strength: cash of USD 734.94 million exceeds debt of USD 491.42 million, the undrawn revolving facility adds USD 345 million and liquidity is USD 1,079.94 million, so the only debt, due in 2034, can be met from cash on hand with USD 234.94 million to spare and any 2026 to 2027 shortfall in free cash flow would be absorbed without borrowing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B7; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margins have been rising on price: operating margin went from 7.48% in 2023 to 10.94% in 2025 and Subsea Robotics from 23.16% to 30.06%, which lifts cash generation per unit of activity and supports debt service if prices hold.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B1; calculation B2; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 112–113

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scale and technology give the company a defensible position, on its own account: it states it is the largest owner and operator of work-class ROVs in energy use, and its umbilicals, subsea hardware, inspection and defense engineering spread revenue over five segments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Backlog and government demand support visibility: firm backlog of USD 2,703 million is 0.97x of 2025 revenue and Aerospace and Defense holds USD 658 million of unfunded orders, which cushions the first year of any downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy is restrained: no dividend since 2017, repurchases of USD 75.37 million paid from cash flow, and no sponsor to extract value, which keeps cash available to creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings are cyclical and concentrated: Subsea Robotics earns 52.03% of segment operating income, ROV utilization has slipped to 64% from 66%, and fourth-quarter operating income is guided lower in that segment and in Offshore Projects Group, so a drop in offshore spending reaches the profit center first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B3; calculation B4; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weaker segments and orders: Integrity Management & Digital Solutions earned a margin of 3.78% in 2025 and Manufactured Products backlog fell 23.42% in the twelve months to 2026-09-30, so two of five segments are not carrying growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B2; calculation B10; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash conversion is volatile and depends on working capital: 2026 free cash flow is guided 42.26% to 51.89% below 2025, contract liabilities of USD 135.30 million equal 18.41% of cash and receivables absorbed USD 139.06 million in nine months, so operating cash flow can swing quickly with collections and prepayments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B5; calculation B8; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The legal structure is not shown: the ranking, guarantors and security of the 2034 notes are not stated, and purchase obligations of USD 410.53 million, lease payments of USD 453.08 million and letters of credit of USD 77 million sit outside the debt figure.

fields.value: - Near-term momentum is flat: fourth-quarter EBITDA is guided at USD 85 million to USD 95 million against USD 87.77 million a year earlier, so the implied 2026 adjusted EBITDA of USD 402.54 million to USD 412.54 million is level with the last twelve months and growth rests on the 2027 guide.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Oceaneering is a Delaware corporation organized in 1969 that rents and builds subsea robots and engineered equipment for offshore oil and gas customers and supplies defense and space engineering to the US Government. Energy customers generate 83.48% of revenue and Aerospace and Defense Technologies 16.52%. Most energy services are priced on dayrates under contracts of under a year to several years, product sales are at fixed prices and the segments' seasonality is mild outside Subsea Robotics and the US Gulf. The model supports debt service because revenue follows days worked on contracts with oil and gas producers and a government customer, but it ties cash flow to offshore activity, which is cyclical.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Oceaneering is a listed company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified, a board that reviews the dividend each quarter, and certain wholly owned subsidiaries that guarantee the secured revolving facility. With no sponsor there is no fee leakage or fund-life exit pressure to price, so risk comes from the board's own policy on buybacks and acquisitions, which has been restrained; the credit agreement and indenture that would limit distributions and secured debt are not supplied, so the legal capacity of the group to move value is not assessed here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical, partly contracted and concentrated in oil and gas producers. Volume comes from ROV days used, which gave a utilization of 65% in 2025 against 67%, and from project work in the Offshore Projects Group; price comes from day rates, which rose in 2026, and from project mix. The five largest customers were 31% of 2025 revenue and the US Government 12%, so a loss of one customer would matter in the short run; contracts can be terminated and backlog is reduced if they are. Pricing power is shown by margins rising while volume slipped, but it rests on offshore demand holding and is less evident in Integrity Management & Digital Solutions, where the margin was 3.78%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B2; calculation B4; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost of services and products was 79.58% of 2025 revenue and unallocated corporate expenses 6.81%, with depreciation and amortization of 3.67%; segment costs include payroll, subcontractors, vessel and equipment rent, maintenance and insurance, while the company expects unallocated expenses of about USD 50 million a quarter in 2026 on wage, technology and currency costs. Vessel charters out to 2029 and a fixed ROV fleet make a large share of cost fixed when utilization falls, so margins defend poorly against volume pressure, even though they have risen despite wage and technology cost increases and raw materials come from multiple sources. One point of ROV utilization is about USD 10.75 million of annual ROV revenue before any cost effect.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B4; calculation B14; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending was 3.99% of 2025 revenue and 1.09x depreciation and amortization, and is guided at USD 105 million to USD 115 million for 2026; management cites about USD 39 million of maintenance and about USD 22 million of growth capital spending in the first nine months, so part of the spend is discretionary. Free cash flow was 51.77% of adjusted EBITDA in 2025 and 70.61% over the last twelve months, but the fourth quarter of 2025 alone supplied USD 190.69 million, and the 2026 guide of USD 100 million to USD 120 million is 24.84% to 29.09% of implied adjusted EBITDA, with third-quarter free cash flow helped by lower tax payments and capital spend. Working capital is the swing factor, and operating leases for vessels and facilities of USD 453.08 million and purchase obligations of USD 410.53 million are fixed claims on cash outside the debt figure; free cash flow is guided to stay positive but at about half of the 2025 level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B5; calculation B6; calculation B8; calculation B11; calculation B14; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is moderate to high: the company is one of several providers of ROV, survey, umbilical and vessel services, small competitors have bid at prices the company calls uneconomical on simple work and umbilicals have been over-supplied, though competitors' capacity reductions are helping; that limits pricing outside ROV services and is consistent with the thin margins in Integrity Management & Digital Solutions. The threat of new entrants appears low in ROV services given fleet scale, the safety record the company cites and the skilled personnel it must retain, and the Jones Act partly protects the US Gulf vessel market, though competitors can move vessels in easily elsewhere. Buyer power is high: oil and gas producers award energy contracts by competitive bid, the top five customers are 31% of revenue and the US Government is 12%. Supplier power is moderate: raw materials are available from several sources and vessels are chartered on a mix of long-term, short-term and spot terms, so cost pressure is manageable but charter cost is fixed to 2029 for part of the fleet. The threat of substitutes comes from autonomous and remote systems, including the company's own AUV and electric ROV, and in the long run from lower offshore energy demand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors matter: uncertainty over US offshore leasing and tariff policy affects US Gulf activity and export costs, local-content rules in some countries favor local contractors, and US defense budgets drive the Aerospace and Defense segment, whose revenue rose 20.18% in nine months. Economic factors are the main driver: oil and gas prices set offshore spending, and foreign operations at 58.75% of nine-month revenue expose results to local currencies, though contracts are primarily denominated in US dollars. Technological change is mostly an opportunity through autonomous and electric systems. Social factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver in the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: net cash and liquidity, margin gains led by Subsea Robotics, the ROV fleet and technology breadth, firm backlog and a restrained financial policy. Weaknesses: earnings concentrated in one segment, thin Integrity Management & Digital Solutions margins, a declining Manufactured Products backlog, working-capital sensitivity, and an unstated ranking of the notes. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: projected growth in subsea tree awards, higher day rates, defense and space demand with USD 658 million of unfunded Aerospace and Defense orders, and the 2027 EBITDA guide. Threats that could weaken it: an oil price fall that cuts offshore spending, lower US Gulf activity, Middle East conflict effects on inspection work, tariffs and trade policy, and a debt-funded acquisition or buyback.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile is stronger than the business profile. Liquidity and financial policy are strong: cash exceeds debt, liquidity is USD 1,079.94 million and distributions are restrained. Free cash flow stability is average to weak: it was USD 207.85 million in 2025 and 70.61% of adjusted EBITDA over twelve months, but 2026 is guided at USD 100 million to USD 120 million. Margin stability is average: the operating margin rose to 10.94% in 2025, yet it follows utilization and day rates. Scale is average to strong with revenue growth of 4.62% in 2025, diversification is average because Subsea Robotics earns 52.03% of segment operating income, and cost and capex flexibility is average because capital spending is partly discretionary but charters and the fleet are fixed. Access to capital markets is strong on the evidence of the July 2026 refinancing, but no rating or bond price is supplied. The trend is improving on margins and liquidity and flat on near-term earnings; the missing data are the ranking of the notes, covenant ratios, the total of letters of credit after 2025-12-31 and a peer set.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B1; calculation B3; calculation B5; calculation B7; calculation B14; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In the next year or two the evidence points to flat 2026 earnings and a step up in 2027 if guidance is met: implied 2026 adjusted EBITDA is USD 402.54 million to USD 412.54 million against USD 408.03 million for the last twelve months, and 2027 is guided at USD 430 million to USD 480 million with free cash flow expected to exceed 2026, which is itself guided 42.26% to 51.89% below 2025. Company-specific tailwinds are firm backlog, Aerospace and Defense growth of 20.18% in nine months with USD 658 million of unfunded orders, higher ROV day rates and cash that funds buybacks without borrowing; headwinds are lower US Gulf activity, a weaker Manufactured Products order book, a Middle East conflict that has held down Integrity Management & Digital Solutions, and lower fourth-quarter operating income in Subsea Robotics and Offshore Projects Group. Sector indicators cited by the company are mixed, with contracted floating rigs down 6.2% in 2025 and projected tree awards 61.05% higher in 2026. Over the medium term the offshore cycle, the long-run demand for oil and gas and defense budgets decide earnings, and the evidence supplied does not support a quantified view beyond 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside is a cut in offshore oil and gas spending that follows a fall in oil prices. The first operational break is fewer drill-support days and less US Gulf project work, which lowers ROV utilization from 64% and stalls day rates; one point of utilization is about USD 10.75 million of annual revenue at the third-quarter rate, and the Manufactured Products order book, already at a book-to-bill of 0.77x, would not refill. Fixed vessel charters, the ROV fleet and unallocated costs mean margin falls faster than revenue. Cash flow would then weaken through lower EBITDA and slower collections, because receivables and contract assets already absorbed USD 139.06 million in nine months and contract liabilities of USD 135.30 million could reverse. Liquidity appears able to absorb this: cash of USD 734.94 million exceeds the USD 500 million of notes, the USD 345 million facility is undrawn and the notes' annual coupon is USD 34.38 million, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through a cyclical downturn; the exposures are a leveraged response by management, such as borrowing to buy back shares, and an unfavorable ranking of the notes, neither of which the sources show. Management levers are lower growth capital spending, cutting buybacks and slower charter renewals; the observable triggers are utilization below 64%, fourth-quarter EBITDA below USD 85 million and any revolver drawing. The margin effect and a full stress are not calculated because incremental margins are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B4; calculation B7; calculation B8; calculation B10; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_oii-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oii-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32–35; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_exhibit_991x8kx3qx2026.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Oceaneering presents an adequate business profile supported by the largest work-class ROV fleet by its own account, firm backlog and government-backed Aerospace and Defense demand, but credit quality is constrained by earnings concentrated in Subsea Robotics, offshore cyclicality and a thin Manufactured Products order book. Cash-flow durability appears adequate, not strong: free cash flow was USD 207.85 million in 2025 but is guided at USD 100 million to USD 120 million for 2026 on working-capital and other operating outflows, and it depends on collections. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the offshore cycle and the ranking of the notes rather than on leverage, since the only debt is due in 2034 and the revolving facility runs to 2031 undrawn. Compared with typical leveraged offshore services issuers the profile is conservatively financed but more concentrated, a qualitative comparison because no peer set is supplied. The primary downside path is a cut in offshore spending that lowers ROV utilization and margins in Subsea Robotics. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and indenture, covenant ratios, the total of letters of credit and a peer set. Top risk: an offshore spending downturn concentrated in Subsea Robotics.
